tagline.text: Hagnaya port for Bantayan and the longest coastline in Cebu

location.label: Location
location.text: San Remigio, northern Cebu Island (about 108 km north of Cebu City)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–4,000 (per person, one night, lodging and transport included)

children.text: San Remigio has the longest shoreline of any municipality in Cebu and is home to Hagnaya port, where ferries to Bantayan Island depart. Beach resorts, marine sanctuaries and the first replica of the Fatima chapel in Asia give you plenty to enjoy in a day or two.
San Remigio lies about
108 km

north of Cebu City. It covers about 95 km² and has 27 barangays and roughly 68,000 residents (2024 census). According to Wikipedia it has the longest coastline of any municipality in Cebu, so small beaches and resorts line one coastal barangay after another. The most populous is the town proper, Poblacion, with about 5,300 residents.

Its old name was "Kanghagas," after a tree that grew abundantly here. The Spanish cleared these trees to mark out the town site; it began as a small village under Bantayan, and in 1850 the parish of Bogo took over its administration. It was later called "Isabel" in honor of Queen Isabella II, renamed San Remigio in 1863, and in 1864 the parish of San Juan Nepomuceno was founded. In 2012 an archaeological team excavated a burial site believed to date from the 1500s.

For travelers, San Remigio's biggest significance is Hagnaya port. Ferries to Santa Fe on Bantayan Island leave here frequently, and boats to Cawayan and Placer in Masbate also depart from this port. Many people only pass through the port, but around it and along the northern and southern coasts there are fine-sand beaches and resorts that make a good place to stay overnight.
Another sight is the Replica de Capelinha de Fatima on Tinubdan Hills in the Tacup-Lambusan area (Wikipedia says Barangay Tacup, local news says Barangay Lambusan). It is reported to be about
13 km

by car from the town. Blessed in April 2022, it is described as the first replica in Asia and the only one in the Philippines. The ability to combine a beach rest with a pilgrimage site in one itinerary is a distinctive feature of this municipality. However, the September 30, 2025 northern Cebu earthquake caused heavy damage in San Remigio too. Wikipedia and early disaster-agency counts (NDRRMC, early October 2025) say 22 of the 72 deaths from that quake occurred here, though some later reports gave different figures. Recovery may still be under way, so check road and facility conditions before you visit. For travelers touring northern Cebu, this municipality is the front door to Bantayan. If you leave Cebu City early in the morning, you can catch a boat at Hagnaya around noon, and on the way back from Bantayan you can rest a night at a beach here. The commercial area around the port is small, but it has restaurants and small shops where you can handle simple needs. You can reach the town from the port by tricycle and similar transport. Check routes and fares locally.
This is the main departure point for ferries to Santa Fe on Bantayan Island. According to 2026 information, Super Shuttle Ferry departs about eight times a day from
at dawn to
in the afternoon, and the crossing takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Boarding lines can get long just before departure.

Casa Del Mar, Elegant Beach Resort, San Remigio Beach Club and Hagnaya Beach Resort are among those on the coast. Each resort has swimming and relaxing facilities, so they are convenient places to stay before or after Bantayan.

blocks.title: Diving at San Remigio Beach Club

children.text: There are several marine sanctuaries off the municipality, and San Remigio Beach Club is said to have a PADI dive shop. For diving or snorkeling, ask the shop directly about prices and sites. Fishing and gathering are restricted inside sanctuaries, so follow the guidance.

The replica of the Fatima chapel in the Tacup-Lambusan area is known as the first in Asia and the only one in the Philippines. It is a quiet shrine visited by many pilgrims, so please observe dress and etiquette when you go. About
30 minutes to 1 hour
is enough to look around it slowly.
There are public beaches around the municipality that you can use without staying at a resort. On weekends many local families visit, and on weekdays it is quiet.

blocks.title: Town center and San Juan Nepomuceno church

children.text: The area around the town church, where the parish was founded in 1864, is the heart of the town. The market and small eateries are clustered here, which makes it a good place to snack and watch local life.
Boats to Cawayan and Placer in Masbate also leave from Hagnaya. As a sea link between the Visayas and Luzon, it is visited by many long-distance travelers.
Walking along the coast at sunset, when the sun goes down over the Tañon Strait to the west, the sky turns red. Just watching the sunset from the beach in front of your lodging fills the day.

Island Shipping and Super Shuttle Ferry link Hagnaya and Santa Fe. As of May 2026 the regular adult fare is about

Use a tricycle or habal-habal between the town, the beaches and Tacup.
To cover several places in a day, hiring a vehicle with a driver is efficient.
For both beaches and boats, the dry season from December to May is best. The sea is calm, ferries run reliably, and conditions for swimming and snorkeling are good.
In the rainy season it rains often and typhoons can cancel boats. If your Bantayan dates are fixed, leave a spare day on either side.

Lodging centers on beach resorts near Hagnaya port and along the coastline. Travelers catching a dawn boat will find a place near the port convenient, while those who want to relax will prefer a quieter beach farther away. Book early in high season.

Grilled fish, shrimp and squid at resort restaurants and Filipino home cooking at town restaurants are the basics. At the market you can buy fruit and snacks cheaply. You can buy snacks and water for the wait at the port, but prices may be slightly higher.
There are no big supermarkets or malls, so it is best to bring any medicine or necessities from Cebu City beforehand.

When choosing a resort, check whether the beach is a swimmable sandy shore or has reef and many stones. Even within one municipality the shoreline differs from barangay to barangay, and at some the bottom is exposed at low tide. Check reviews and recent photos, and if needed message the lodging to ask about tides and swimming conditions.
Ferry lines to Bantayan get long in high season, so get to the port early.
If you are crossing with a vehicle, the vehicle fare is charged separately, so check beforehand.
If you want to take a dawn boat from Hagnaya, it is convenient to stay near the port the night before.
Put cameras and electronics in a waterproof pouch. Spray sometimes splashes on the boat.
The Fatima chapel is a holy place, so modest dress covering shoulders and knees is recommended.
Bring plenty of cash. Many restaurants and stalls do not take cards.
Check the latest ferry fares and times in the operator's announcements.
The road from Hagnaya into town has many motorbikes, so it is safer to use a vehicle when carrying large luggage.
The September 30, 2025 Cebu earthquake caused heavy loss of life in this municipality. Check the current recovery situation and accessibility in local government announcements.
In the rainy and typhoon seasons, boats may be canceled because of sea conditions.
Some beaches have no lifeguards, so ask locals where it is safe to swim.
Public transport is almost nonexistent at dawn and at night, so arrange your transfers between the port and lodging in advance.
In sanctuaries, do not step on or touch the coral.
